description.description: What belongs to the class, in words.

label_value.description: Pixel value of the class in semantic masks. Not used for instance masks, where each object has its own value.

name.description: Name of the class, e.g. nucleus.

ontology_term.description: IRI of an ontology term for the class, e.g. a CL or GO term.

AnnotationMethod.description: How much of the annotation was done by people and how much by software.
AnnotationMethod.title: AnnotationMethod

AnnotationRecord.description: One annotation of a set: the image region it covers, its split, its state and its files. Flat, so a table of records is a CSV file with one column per field (well_metadata and external_ids as JSON text).

annotation_id.description: Identifier of the annotation, unique within the set. Files are named after it.

annotation_type.description: Kind of annotation, using MIFA's values.

external_ids.description: Identifiers of copies in other systems as a JSON object, e.g. {"omero_roi":"123","omero_label_image":"456"}.

image_iscc.description: ISCC code of the whole source image, made as declared in the set's content_codes.image - for example the ISCC-SUM (IMAGEWALK) that omero-iscc stores on OMERO images. Identifies the source by content, whatever its URI.

image_name.description: Name of the source image, for people.

image_uri.description: The source image - omero:image:<id>, an http(s) URL of an OME-Zarr image, or another resolvable URI.

input_digest.description: Pixel SHA-256 of the annotated image region.

input_file.description: Path of the annotated image region, relative to the set's folder.

input_iscc.description: ISCC code of the annotated image region, made as declared in the set's content_codes.region.

level.description: Multiscale level the coordinates refer to (0 = full resolution).

mask_file.description: Path of the mask, relative to the set's folder.

mask_iscc.description: ISCC code of the mask, made as declared in the set's content_codes.region.

patch_height.description: Height of the patch in pixels.

patch_width.description: Width of the patch in pixels.

patch_x.description: Left edge of the patch in pixels, at the given level.

patch_y.description: Top edge of the patch in pixels, at the given level.

session.description: id of the session (in the set) that last saved this annotation.

transformations.description: Transformations needed to align the annotation with the source image, e.g. a rotation or crop.

updated_at.description: When the annotation was last changed.

well_metadata.description: Key-value metadata of the well as a JSON object, e.g. {"cell_line":"U2OS"}.

z_end.description: Last z-slice of a volumetric annotation (inclusive).

z_start.description: First z-slice of a volumetric annotation.

AnnotationRecord.title: AnnotationRecord

AnnotationSet.description: A set of image annotations for AI: one document per set. The annotations themselves are AnnotationRecords, usually kept as a CSV table next to it.

ai_models_trained.description: AI models trained on these annotations, by DOI or URL (e.g. a BioImage Model Zoo entry).

authors.description: Authors of the set, in citation order.

changes.description: What changed since the previous version.

classes.description: The annotation classes (e.g. nucleus, cell, background).

content_codes.description: How the ISCC codes in the records were made. Required when any record has input_iscc, mask_iscc or image_iscc: codes are only comparable when they were made the same way.

description.description: What the set contains and what it is for, in a few sentences.

extensions.description: Tool- or project-specific metadata this schema does not cover, under a namespace key such as the tool name.

keywords.description: Keywords or tags that describe the set.

license.description: License of the annotations. Only the two licences the BioImage Archive accepts are allowed.

links.description: Web pages about the set or its data, e.g. a repository or a project page.

normalization.description: Intensity normalisation intended for model input.

notes.description: Free text - context, caveats, known issues.

previous_version.description: Identifier (DOI or URL) of the previous version of the set.

sampling.description: Which channels, planes and regions of the images were annotated.

schema_version.description: Version of this schema the document follows (semantic versioning).

sessions.description: Annotation sessions, oldest first. Records refer to them by id.

source_dataset.description: The image dataset the annotated images come from.

split.description: How the annotations were divided over training, validation and test.

study.description: The biological and experimental context of the images.

version.description: Version of this set, e.g. "1" or "1.1".

AnnotationSet.title: AnnotationSet

CodeMethod.description: How one kind of ISCC code was computed.

bits.description: Length of the code's body in bits, e.g. 64 for an Image-Code unit, 128 or 256 (wide) for an ISCC-SUM.

implementation.description: Software and version that computed the codes, e.g. 'omero-annotate-ai 0.6.0 (iscc-lib 0.7.1)'.

pixels.description: Which pixels were coded, e.g. 'the annotated region as saved in input_file' or 'all planes of the source image'.

preparation.description: What was done to the pixels before coding: plane order and byte encoding, projection, resizing, intensity scaling, mask binarisation. 'none' if the stored pixels were coded as they are.

specification.description: The specification the preparation follows, if any, e.g. https://ieps.iscc.codes/iep-0018/ (IMAGEWALK) for bioimage ISCC-SUMs.

CodeMethod.title: CodeMethod

ContentCodes.description: How the ISCC codes (ISO 24138) in the records were made. ISCC is a family of codes: the same image gives different codes depending on the code type, which pixels are coded and how they are prepared, so each kind is declared here.

image.description: How image_iscc (the code of the whole source image) was made.

region.description: How input_iscc and mask_iscc were made.

ContentCodes.title: ContentCodes

Coverage.description: How completely the objects in an annotated region are annotated.
Coverage.title: Coverage

Grant.description: A grant that funded the study.
Grant.title: Grant

IsccCodeType.description: ISCC code types used for images.
IsccCodeType.title: IsccCodeType

License.description: Licenses the BioImage Archive accepts for annotations.
License.title: License

Link.description: A web page about the set or its data.
Link.title: Link

MaskKind.description: How pixel values in a segmentation mask are assigned.
MaskKind.title: MaskKind

annotation_types.description: Kinds of annotation in the set, using MIFA's values.

annotators.description: People who made or reviewed the annotations, if different from the set's authors.

confidence_level.description: Confidence in the annotations' accuracy, e.g. annotator experience or inter-annotator agreement.

coverage.description: Within an annotated region, whether all objects are annotated, a representative selection, or only some.

coverage_description.description: Which images were annotated and what share of the dataset, in words.

criteria.description: What counts as an object and where its boundary is, in words.

mask_kind.description: For segmentation masks - one value per object (instance) or per class (semantic).

method.description: Whether annotations were drawn by hand, proposed by software and corrected, or made by software alone.

method_description.description: How the annotations were created, in words: who, which software, consensus and quality checks.

overview.description: Short summary of the type of annotation and how it was made.

tools.description: Software used to make the annotations.

Model.description: An AI model that proposed annotations.

name.description: Name of the model, e.g. vit_b_lm.

url.description: Where the model can be found, e.g. a BioImage Model Zoo page.

Model.title: Model

Normalization.description: Intensity normalisation intended for model input.

clip.description: True if values outside [0, 1] are clipped.

Normalization.title: Normalization

Organisation.description: An organisation a person is affiliated with.

ror.description: ROR identifier as URL, e.g. https://ror.org/027bh9e22.

Organisation.title: Organisation

Patches.description: Present if annotations cover patches rather than whole planes.

per_image.description: Number of patches per image plane.

random.description: True if patch positions were drawn at random, false if they tile the plane.

Patches.title: Patches

Person.description: A person: an author of the set or an annotator.

affiliations.description: Organisations the person is affiliated with.

last_name.description: Family name, with particles such as "van der".

roles.description: Roles in the work, e.g. annotator, data curator.

Person.title: Person

PlaneSelection.description: Which timepoints or z-slices were annotated.

n.description: How many were drawn, for mode 'random'.

PlaneSelection.title: PlaneSelection

Publication.description: A publication associated with the study.

authors.description: Author list as written in the reference.

Publication.title: Publication

Sampling.description: Which parts of the images were annotated. Per-annotation detail is in the records.

input_channels.description: Channels meant as model input; may differ from label_channel (annotate on a nuclear stain, train on brightfield).

label_channel.description: Channel the annotations were drawn on.

patches.description: Patch size and number, if annotations cover patches.

volumetric.description: True if annotations are 3D volumes rather than 2D planes.

Sampling.title: Sampling

SelectionMode.description: How timepoints or z-slices were chosen.
SelectionMode.title: SelectionMode

Session.description: One annotation session - who, when, with what, and a note.

annotator.description: Who annotated - a name, ORCID or pseudonym.

ended.description: When the session ended; absent while it is open.

id.description: Number of the session within the set, from 0.

kind.description: 'annotate' creates annotations, 'review' checks or corrects them.

model.description: Name of the AI model used in the session, if any.

n_annotated.description: Number of annotations saved in the session.

Session.title: Session

SourceDataset.description: The image dataset the annotated images come from.

description.description: What the source images are, in words.

identifier.description: Accession or DOI, e.g. S-BIAD123 or idr0001.

license.description: License of the source images, e.g. CC-BY-4.0.

url.description: Web page or download address of the dataset.

SourceDataset.title: SourceDataset

Split.description: How annotations were divided over training, validation and test.

rationale.description: Why this unit, e.g. 'fields within a well do not overlap'.

seed.description: Seed of the random choices, to reproduce the selection with the same tool.

stratify_by.description: Metadata keys the split was balanced on (e.g. cell_line, treatment).

unit.description: Level at which data are assigned to a split; all annotations of one unit share a split. 'image' or 'well', or another level named by the tool.

Split.title: Split

SplitStrategy.description: How annotations were assigned to splits.
SplitStrategy.title: SplitStrategy

Study.description: Biological and experimental context of the images.

description.description: Brief description of the study, including the biological application of the images.

funding_statement.description: How the study was funded, in words.

imaging_method.description: Imaging method, e.g. confocal fluorescence microscopy.

organism.description: Organism the samples come from, e.g. Homo sapiens.

title.description: Title of the study; often the title of the associated publication.

Study.title: Study

Tool.description: Software used to make the annotations.

model.description: The AI model the software used, if any.

name.description: Name of the software, e.g. micro-sam or cellpose.

parameters.description: Settings the software ran with, as the tool names them.
